info.description: File-storage API — per-tenant S3/GCS/Storj buckets + file ops, federated identity via enforcer-v3.
info.title: enforcer-files API

get.description: The OCR queue of files flagged wants_ocr that have not been OCR'd. System-admin only. The OCR worker's service key drains every tenant and CLAIMS the rows it is given. Anyone else sees their own tenant's queue by default, another tenant with tenant_id, or every tenant with all_tenants=true (cross_tenant grant), and claims nothing. tenant_id together with all_tenants=true is a 400.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (default 20)

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Pagination offset (ignored for the worker, whose read claims the queue head)

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: Confine the queue to this tenant (another tenant needs cross_tenant)

parameters.name: all_tenants
parameters.description: Every tenant's queue (cross_tenant grant); implicit only for the OCR worker

get.description: Streams the raw source object for a queued file. System-admin only. Same tenant scope as the queue: the OCR worker's service key reaches any tenant; anyone else reaches their own tenant's files unless they send tenant_id=<the file's tenant> or all_tenants=true (cross_tenant grant). A file outside the scope is a 403 cross_tenant_file.
get.summary: Download source bytes for an OCR job (admin)

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description: File ID

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The file's tenant, when it is not the caller's own (cross_tenant)

parameters.name: all_tenants
parameters.description: Reach a file in any tenant (cross_tenant grant)

post.description: Stores the request body at the predictable .ocr/<file_id>.json key in the file's own backend/bucket, sets is_ocr, and records the output key in ocr_output. System-admin only. Same tenant scope as the queue: the OCR worker's service key reaches any tenant; anyone else reaches their own tenant's files unless they send tenant_id=<the file's tenant> or all_tenants=true (cross_tenant grant). A file outside the scope is a 403 cross_tenant_file.
post.summary: Submit OCR result for a file (admin)

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description: File ID

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: The file's tenant, when it is not the caller's own (cross_tenant)

parameters.name: all_tenants
parameters.description: Reach a file in any tenant (cross_tenant grant)

get.description: Lists GCS buckets for the configured project. System-admin only.

post.description: Creates a new GCS bucket. System-admin only.

delete.description: Deletes the named GCS bucket. System-admin only.

parameters.name: bucket_name
parameters.description: Bucket name

get.description: Lists S3 buckets visible to the resolved credentials. System-admin only.

post.description: Creates a new S3 bucket. System-admin only.

delete.description: Deletes the named S3 bucket. System-admin only.

parameters.name: bucket_name
parameters.description: Bucket name

get.description: Lists Storj buckets reachable with the tenant's access grant. System-admin only.

post.description: Creates a new Storj bucket. System-admin only.

delete.description: Deletes the named Storj bucket. System-admin only.

parameters.name: bucket_name
parameters.description: Bucket name

put.description: Validates the service-account credentials against the bucket (creating it if missing) and saves the tenant's GCS connection config. Rejects with 400 storage_unreachable when they cannot reach the bucket. System and tenant admins only.
put.summary: Set the per-tenant GCS storage connection

put.description: Validates the credentials against the bucket (HeadBucket, creating it if missing) and saves the tenant's S3 connection config. Rejects with 400 storage_unreachable when the credentials cannot sign or reach the bucket. System and tenant admins only.
put.summary: Set the per-tenant S3 storage connection

put.description: Validates the access grant against the bucket (creating it if missing) and saves the tenant's Storj connection config. Rejects with 400 storage_unreachable when it cannot open the project or reach the bucket. System and tenant admins only.
put.summary: Set the per-tenant Storj storage connection

get.description: Reports whether the given provider is configured for the tenant, secrets masked, and probes the stored credentials against the bucket. Read `status`: "unconfigured" means no connection is saved (not a fault), "healthy" means the stored credentials just reached the bucket, "unhealthy" means they did not and health_error says why. A connection saved with a secret that cannot sign is therefore visible here rather than on a user's first upload. System and tenant admins only.
get.summary: Get a per-tenant storage connection status (secrets masked)

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Storage provider

delete.description: Removes the tenant's stored connection config for the given provider. System and tenant admins only.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Storage provider

get.description: Lists the caller's stored GCS files from the metadata index, paginated. owner_group_id / exclude_owner_group_id slice the listing by who owns each file; each row carries owner_id.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Directory to list, exact match ('/' for the root). Omit to list every file regardless of directory. Trashed files are never listed.

parameters.name: delimiter
parameters.description: Set to / to also return directories (the immediate child directories under path) and directory_stats (per folder, same order: recursive file_count, total_bytes, latest updated_at).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (1-100, default 20)

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Pagination offset

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Admin only: act on behalf of this user ID

parameters.name: owner_group_id
parameters.description: Only files whose owner (uploader) is a member of this group (uuid). Not files shared WITH the group: that is GET /storage/group/{group_id}/files. Without owner, spans every member the caller may read: all of them for a caller who may read any file in the tenant, otherwise only the caller. Narrows only. Applies to meta.total, total_bytes and directory_stats too. 404 when the group is unknown or not visible to the caller.

parameters.name: exclude_owner_group_id
parameters.description: Drop files whose owner is a member of this group (uuid). Same scope rules and 404 as owner_group_id; combinable with it.

delete.description: Deletes a file by file_id: the object and its metadata row. Trashed files are deleted permanently.

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description: File ID to delete when the request has no body

parameters.name: object_key
parameters.description: Legacy: object key relative to the caller namespace (object only, no row)

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Admin only: act on behalf of this user ID

requestBody.description: file_id (or legacy object_key) to delete; may be omitted in favour of the query parameters

409.description: file_in_folder: a file in a folder changes only through the /storage/folders routes

post.description: Copies a file (by file_id) to a new path within the caller's namespace and records a new row. destination_path may include directories.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Admin only: act on behalf of this user ID

requestBody.description: file_id of the source and destination_path (relative path, may include directories, e.g. invoices/2026/a.pdf)

get.description: Streams a stored GCS object by file_id (ownership-checked) or direct object key.

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description: File ID (preferred; validates ownership)

parameters.name: object_key
parameters.description: Direct object key (alternative to file_id)

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Admin only: act on behalf of this user ID

post.description: Moves a file (by file_id) to a new path within the caller's namespace and updates its row. destination_path may include directories.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Admin only: act on behalf of this user ID

requestBody.description: file_id of the source and destination_path (relative path, may include directories, e.g. invoices/2026/a.pdf)

post.description: Moves the given files (by file_id) to the .trash/ prefix and hides them from listings, or deletes them permanently along with their rows.
post.summary: Move files to trash or delete them in GCS

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Admin only: act on behalf of this user ID

409.description: file_in_folder: a file in a folder changes only through the /storage/folders routes

post.description: Uploads a file to GCS under the caller's tenant/user prefix, with optional server-side image processing.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Admin only: act on behalf of this user ID

file_name.description: Target path relative to your namespace, e.g. invoices/2026/a.pdf. Slashes create directories; '..' and absolute paths are rejected. Defaults to the multipart filename.

directory.description: Directory to place the file under (prepended to file_name's directory, if any).

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at the same path and refresh its row. Without it a same-path upload returns 409.

process_image.description: Set to true/1 to downscale, re-encode and strip metadata server-side (images only, max 15 MiB)

image_kind.description: Processing bounds: logo, banner, thumbnail or photo (default banner). Use photo for photographs — banner is a 1920x640 landscape strip and reduces a portrait phone photo to 480px wide.

post.description: Second half of the presigned upload flow. After the client PUTs the bytes to the URL from presigned-upload-url, it calls this with the same file_name; the service confirms the object exists at the server-derived key, reads its real size, and creates the metadata row that listing, download, move, copy, trash and delete all key off. Without this call a presigned upload lands in the bucket but never appears in the file system. Same-path collisions follow the multipart upload rule: 409 unless overwrite=true, which refreshes the existing row instead.
post.summary: Record a file uploaded through a presigned URL (S3)

requestBody.description: The file_name that was presigned, plus optional row attributes

get.description: Returns a short-lived presigned PUT URL plus the server-derived object key. Upload with an HTTP PUT to the URL, then POST /storage/file/s3/presigned-upload-complete with the same file_name so the file gets its metadata row (until then it is invisible to listing and file_id operations). A same-path row is refused with 409 unless overwrite=true.

parameters.name: file_name
parameters.description: Target path relative to the caller's namespace (e.g. invoices/2026/a.pdf); slashes become the file's directory. Traversal and absolute paths are rejected.

parameters.name: expiry
parameters.description: URL lifetime in seconds (default 900, max 604800)

parameters.name: overwrite
parameters.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the same path (default false)

get.description: Generates a time-limited presigned S3 download URL for an object.
get.summary: Get a presigned S3 download URL

parameters.description: Direct object key (alternative to file_id)

parameters.description: Admin only: act on behalf of this user ID

get.description: Pages the folders the caller can see at any role, by name: their own user folders, folders shared with one of their groups, and (tenant admins) every folder in the tenant. A service principal sees only the folders it manages and must send tenant_id.

parameters.name: parent_id
parameters.description: Only children of this folder; present and empty = root folders only

parameters.name: managed_by
parameters.description: Only folders managed by this service label

parameters.name: managed_ref
parameters.description: Only the folder with this managed ref

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: true = archived only, false = live only; absent = both

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: Service principal only, and required for one

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (default 50, max 200)

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Page offset

post.description: Creates a folder in the caller's tenant. Any member may create a user folder (under a parent they can write). A service principal creates MANAGED folders only: managed_by must equal its service label and, with managed_ref, the call is an ensure — an existing (tenant, managed_by, managed_ref) answers 200 with created:false, so concurrent calls make one folder. A service principal must send tenant_id; an end user must not. quota_bytes is tenant-admin or service only.

get.description: Returns the folder with the caller's role (my_role) and its usage. Requires read on the folder; a folder the caller cannot see is 404, byte-identical to one that does not exist.

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Folder ID

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: Service principal only, and required for one

delete.description: Soft delete: the folder and its subfolders become invisible to every route; their files keep their folder and become unreachable. Needs manage on a user folder; on a managed folder only the managing service. purge=true hard deletes every file row and object in the folder and its subfolders, both share tables' rows, and the folders themselves; it reaches an already soft-deleted folder, and needs a tenant admin (user folders) or the managing service (managed folders).

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Folder ID

parameters.name: purge
parameters.description: Hard delete everything (default false)

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: Service principal only, and required for one

parameters.name: actor_account_id
parameters.description: Service principal only: the human the service acts for

patch.description: Absent fields are unchanged; parent_id "" moves the folder to the root. Rename and move need manage on a user folder, and are the managing service's alone on a managed folder (403 managed_folder). quota_bytes (or clear_quota) needs a tenant admin or the managing service. An archived folder cannot be renamed or moved.
patch.summary: Rename, move or set the quota of a folder

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Folder ID

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: Service principal only, and required for one

post.description: Makes the folder read-only: every write is 409 folder_archived; reads and share management still work. Idempotent. Needs manage on a user folder; on a managed folder only the managing service.

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Folder ID

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: Service principal only, and required for one

parameters.name: actor_account_id
parameters.description: Service principal only: the human the service acts for

get.description: Pages the folder's files, newest first unless sort/sort_dir say otherwise (id is always the final tie-breaker); each row's user_id is its uploader. total counts the rows matching q and path. Requires read on the folder.

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Folder ID

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Only files in this directory within the folder (/ = the folder root); absent = every directory

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of the file name; empty = no filter

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort key (default created_at)

parameters.name: sort_dir
parameters.description: Sort direction (default desc)

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: Service principal only, and required for one

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (default 50, max 200)

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Page offset

post.description: Multipart upload into the folder, as POST /storage/file/s3/upload (no process_image). Requires write on the folder. The object lands under the uploader's own namespace in the folder's path space. A same-path file is 409 unless it is your own upload and overwrite=true; another member's file at that path is 409 file_exists. The size is checked against the folder's quota before anything is written. s3 and house tenants only.
post.summary: Upload a file into a folder

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Folder ID

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: Service principal only, and required for one

parameters.name: actor_account_id
parameters.description: Service principal only: the human the service acts for

file_type.description: Caller-defined type label stored on the row

overwrite.description: Replace YOUR existing file at the same path

wants_ocr.description: Flag the file for the OCR worker (supported types only)

put.description: Moves an existing s3 file into the folder, at the folder root under its own name. Needs write on the target folder AND authority over the file: its owner, manage on the folder it is in now, or a tenant admin. The object is copied to its folder key and the old one deleted. Moving a file into the folder it is already in is a no-op.

get.description: Returns a short-lived presigned GET URL for one file in the folder. Requires read on the folder, and reads anyone's upload in it, not only the caller's. This is the read route a managing service can use: it names the tenant with tenant_id as on every other folder route, which GET /storage/file/s3/presigned-url cannot take. An archived folder is still readable. The URL is signed without checking the object exists; a row whose object is gone answers 404 from storage when the URL is fetched.

get.description: Returns the tenant's active storage provider, where it comes from, and the upload flow it supports ("presigned" = PUT straight to object storage; "proxy" = POST multipart here). source is "tenant" when the tenant configured its own connection and "house" when it has none and the operator's default S3 serves it (provider "s3"); a tenant's own connection of any provider always wins over the house. configured=false means neither exists and uploads will be refused. 503 storage_unavailable means the tenant's own configuration could not be read right now — the service refuses rather than guess. Readable by any authenticated member of the tenant — unlike GET /storage/connection/{provider}, it discloses no endpoint, region, bucket or satellite address.
get.summary: Which storage provider serves this tenant's uploads

source.description:
Source says whose storage it is: "tenant" when the tenant configured
its own connection, "house" when it has none and the operator's default
S3 bucket serves it (always provider "s3"). Empty when Configured is
false. A tenant moves from "house" to "tenant" by saving a connection
of its own; objects already in the house bucket are NOT migrated.

upload_mode.description:
UploadMode tells the caller which upload FLOW this provider supports, so
it does not have to hardcode a provider-to-flow table that drifts:

  "presigned"  — ask for a presigned URL and PUT the bytes straight to
                 object storage (S3).
  "proxy"      — POST multipart to this service, which uploads onward
                 (Storj: native uplink has no presigned URLs, and the
                 S3 gateway would terminate the client-side encryption
                 that is the whole reason uplink was chosen).

healthy.description:
Live probe of the stored credentials against the bucket, run on every
GET (connections saved before the probe existed were never checked).
Healthy is meaningful only when Configured is true; HealthError carries
the provider's reason when Healthy is false. Kept for compatibility —
prefer Status.

status.description:
Status is the ONE field a UI should read: "unconfigured" (no connection
saved for this provider — not a fault), "healthy" (the stored credentials
just passed a live probe against the bucket) or "unhealthy" (they did
not; HealthError says why). It exists because the two booleans below
were misread: an unconfigured provider reports healthy=false, and the
portal painted every tenant's GCS red for a connection that was never
meant to exist.

tenant_id.description: required for system admins; omit to use own tenant

updated_at.description: latest updated_at beneath the folder; null if unknown

folder_id.description:
FolderID is the folder the file belongs to, null for a file in its
uploader's personal namespace (every file uploaded through the
/storage/file/* routes). A foldered file is reached by folder role and
is changed only through the folder routes: the legacy move, trash and
delete by file_id answer 409 file_in_folder for it.

provider.description: Provider is the storage backend the object lives in ("s3"|"gcs"|"storj").

wants_ocr.description:
OCR pipeline flags (see the file entity for semantics). OCROutput is the
full object key of the generated OCR JSON, "" until OCR'd.

directories.description:
Directories is the immediate child folder names under path, present only
when the listing was called with delimiter=/ (S3 CommonPrefixes).

directory_stats.description:
DirectoryStats is one entry per Directories name, in the same order,
present only with delimiter=/. Counts are recursive.

url.description:
URL is the permanent public CDN URL for the object. Only populated
when the upload was server-side processed (process_image=true) AND
the tenant has an S3 CDN configured (cdn_root_url on its s3
connection); empty otherwise, so existing callers are unaffected.
Unlike PresignedURL — which is short-TTL and scoped to the file's
own owner — this URL is unauthenticated and renderable by anyone,
which is what makes it usable as an avatar/profile picture source.

file_name.description: FileName is the same value passed to presigned-upload-url.

file_type.description: FileType is an optional caller-defined type label stored on the row.

overwrite.description: Overwrite refreshes an existing row at the same path instead of a 409.

policy_id.description: PolicyID is an optional policy to attach to the row.

wants_ocr.description: WantsOCR flags the file for the OCR worker (supported types only).

actor_account_id.description:
ActorAccountID: service only; the human the service acts for, recorded
as the activity actor (without it the event is admin-only).

managed_by.description:
ManagedBy must equal the calling service's label (403 managed_folder
otherwise, and for any human). With ManagedRef it makes the create an
ensure: an existing managed key answers 200 created:false.

owner_account_id.description: OwnerAccountID: service only; attribution, grants nothing on a managed folder.

quota_bytes.description: QuotaBytes: tenant admin or service only. 0 = no cap.

tenant_id.description:
TenantID: service principal only, and required for one
(400 tenant_id_not_allowed for an end user).

file_count.description: FileCount and TotalBytes count the folder's non-deleted files.

my_role.description: MyRole is the caller's role: read | write | manage | service.

provider.description: Provider is the storage backend the object lives in ("s3"|"gcs"|"storj").

wants_ocr.description:
OCR pipeline flags (see the file entity for semantics). OCROutput is the
full object key of the generated OCR JSON, "" until OCR'd.

all_tenants.description: AllTenants is true when the page covers every tenant's queue.

claimed.description:
Claimed is true when the rows were leased to this caller (the worker's
service principal); a human's view is a peek and claims nothing.

tenant_id.description: TenantID is the one tenant the page covers, when AllTenants is false.

clear_quota.description: ClearQuota resets quota_bytes to the service default (null).

quota_bytes.description: QuotaBytes: tenant admin or managing service only. 0 = no cap.
